articles.title: Lady Gaga's foundation donates $100,000 to Atlanta youth organisation after awarding it $50,000 in 2024; the money is helping students access mental health support, education and essential resources
articles.summary: Lady Gaga's philanthropic organisation has donated $100,000 to an Atlanta-based nonprofit that provides young people with mental health support,
articles.body: Lady Gaga's philanthropic organisation has donated $100,000 to an Atlanta-based nonprofit that provides young people with mental health support, educational opportunities and essential resources. The contribution from her Born This Way Foundation went to COR, an organisation working with students and families through school-based programmes. At Carver STEAM Academy and Carver Early College in Atlanta, students can access free counselling, participate in after-school activities, use a community grocery store and receive guidance from social workers. The funding is expected to help COR pay the social workers who provide mental health services to young people. The latest contribution follows an earlier $50,000 grant awarded to the organisation in 2024 through the Kindness in Community Fund.Lady Gaga's foundation makes another contribution to Atlanta nonprofitThe $100,000 donation was made by the Born This Way Foundation, established in 2011 by Lady Gaga and her mother, Cynthia Germanotta. The organisation focuses on supporting young people's mental health, promoting kindness and creating communities where young people feel accepted and supported.The foundation selected COR, an Atlanta nonprofit focused on helping students overcome educational and socioeconomic barriers, as the recipient of the latest contribution.According to CBS News Atlanta, the money will be used to pay social workers who provide services to children through COR's programmes. The contribution was reported on March 5, 2026, during Lady Gaga's Mayhem Ball Tour stop in Atlanta.The latest funding follows a $50,000 grant COR received in July 2024 through the Kindness in Community Fund, an initiative supported by the Born This Way Foundation and Cotton On Foundation. That earlier grant was intended to expand access to behavioural health services and family support programmes.How COR is helping students access mental health supportCOR operates school-based resource centres where students can access free counselling, interact with social workers and seek assistance with personal and emotional challenges.At Carver STEAM Academy and Carver Early College, students can visit the organisation's on-campus space after classes to meet other students, speak with guidance counsellors and participate in activities designed to build relationships.The programme also provides access to social workers who offer free mental health counselling. Students can seek support without having to travel to an external facility or pay for services.During its visit to Carver, CBS News Atlanta spoke with students who described the centre as a place where they could connect with peers from different schools and develop stronger relationships.COR executive director and co-founder Jennifer Henn told the broadcaster that the organisation wanted students to recognise their potential, access new opportunities and learn how to look after themselves.The latest donation is expected to help fund the professionals who make these services available to students.Students can access free groceries, clothing and essential suppliesCOR's work extends beyond mental health counselling. The organisation also operates a free community resource centre called the CORner Store, where students and families can access groceries, clothing, hygiene products and other everyday necessities.Students can also work at the store, gaining practical experience and developing workplace skills while participating in activities outside their regular classes.CBS News Atlanta spoke with Carver student Isaiah Oakes, who said working at the store gave him something productive to do after school and provided a relaxing environment.Parents and caregivers can also access essential resources through the organisation. These include furniture, clothing and other household supplies, helping families manage some of their everyday expenses.The programme is designed to address several challenges that can affect a student's ability to participate in education, including food insecurity and a lack of access to basic necessities.COR also provides education on grief, health and human traffickingThe Atlanta nonprofit conducts educational programmes that help students understand personal safety, recognise potential risks and make informed decisions.Its prevention education classes cover subjects such as health, managing grief, conflict resolution, human trafficking and exploitation. These sessions are designed to help young people recognise warning signs and understand where to seek assistance.COR also works with parents and caregivers, offering financial literacy classes to help families improve their understanding of money management and household finances.The organisation's programmes bring together students, families, educators and social workers to address challenges that can affect young people's development and education.Its approach combines mental health services with practical resources and educational activities rather than focusing on counselling alone.COR reports hundreds of hours of mental health supportCOR's published figures for the 2025–26 school year provide an indication of the scale of its activities across its programmes.According to its official website, the organisation recorded:794 hours of mental health support.1,572 hours of prevention education training.1,736 visits to its CORner Store.These figures cover different aspects of the organisation's work, including direct support for students, educational sessions and access to essential supplies.COR has also expanded its school-based programmes beyond Carver STEAM Academy. In 2024, it announced plans to extend its services to Price Middle School, responding to requests from school administrators for additional mental health and family support resources.How Lady Gaga's foundation supports young people's mental healthThe Born This Way Foundation was established in 2011 by Lady Gaga and Cynthia Germanotta to support young people's mental health and promote kindness and acceptance.One of its initiatives is the Kindness in Community Fund, which provides financial support to grassroots organisations addressing challenges faced by young people in their communities.The programme supports organisations offering direct mental health services as well as assistance related to housing, food security and safety.In 2025, the foundation invested $5 million in 55 youth-centred organisations across 11 countries through the fund. Its funding priorities include organisations that involve young people in decision-making, promote inclusion and provide accessible mental health resources.The foundation also offers the Be There Certificate, a free online educational programme that teaches people how to recognise when someone may be experiencing mental health difficulties, offer support and connect them with appropriate resources.You use AI every day. articles.title: Melania Trump hails Oleshky ceasefire as potential ‘spark’ for progress amid Ukraine-Russia war
articles.summary: Melania Trump called the Oleshky ceasefire "a spark in a world of darkness" as Russian and Ukrainian envoys praised the deal at a rare White House event.
articles.body: First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire. "We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark." "Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity." INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians. Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting. US WILL MEDIATE UPCOMING UKRAINE-RUSSIA TALKS IN ABU DHABI, WITKOFF SAYS "President Putin also appreciates President Trump's peacemaking effort and his team working on a peace plan to resolve Ukrainian crisis," Dmitriev said in a rare moment of a Russian diplomat speaking at the White House. "President Trump has asked President Putin to support a number of initiatives on exchanging of prisoners, on releasing U.S. prisoners on humanitarian efforts. And President Putin supported those ideas and those initiatives." "And it's very important that cooperation between Russia and Ukraine and Russia in the United States matters not only for our two nations, but for the entire world," he continued. "Let us continue making great humanitarian contributions. We can together, let us build a future of peace, partnership and prosperity for the benefit of our families, our children and future generations." RUSSIA RELEASES AMERICAN TEACHER IMPRISONED ON UKRAINE MERCENARY CHARGES AFTER TRUMP PRESSED PUTIN "Dear Melania, you saved and touched so many lives," he concluded. David Arakhamia, the leader of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's political party, called Melania Trump's ceasefire the 'biggest de-escalation since 2022," when the war began. UKRAINE'S ZELENSKYY OPEN TO FREEZING FRONT LINES IN CEASEFIRE WITH RUSSIA "Madam first lady, I would like to thank you: You did an amazing job," he said. "I think when everything started with you and your team, we had about 5% of people who believed in success, and 95% of skeptics who said it wasn’t going to work. Now, after it happened, it’s switched completely: 95% of the people believe that we can do things like that, and 5% are still skeptical." Peace is now a matter of when, not if, he added. KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE Getting fearful Ukrainians out of the Russian-controlled city is an important step toward deciding how peace will be made and determining the long-term fate of the occupied territory of southern Ukraine. "On the first day, people in the area did not believe it was happening," Arakhamia said. "They stayed in their homes, waiting to see if the clock was ticking backward. The next day, they started walking around their homes. The day after that, they came to see their broken homes and find their belongings. "This is really emotional to watch and supervise, to understand what we are doing," he added. "I think we are creating momentum where both sides are learning the little mechanics of how to keep the peace when the peace comes. "I would also like to sincerely thank you, from my heart, for doing this." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Dmitriev attended the event and met with U.S. officials, sources told Reuters. articles.title: Gigi and Bella Hadid spent their childhood in a Malibu mansion that was once listed for $34.99 million; after wildfires destroyed it, the 3.25-acre land parcel sold for $6.5 million
articles.summary: Gigi and Bella Hadid’s childhood home in Malibu has entered a new chapter after the mansion was destroyed by the devastating California wildfires in
articles.body: Gigi and Bella Hadid’s childhood home in Malibu has entered a new chapter after the mansion was destroyed by the devastating California wildfires in January 2025. The property, which once belonged to their mother Yolanda Hadid and her former husband David Foster, had been listed for $34.99 million before the disaster. More than a year after the blaze, its 3.25-acre land parcel has sold for $6.5 million, marking a significant change in the fortunes of an estate once associated with luxury living and family memories.How Gigi and Bella Hadid’s childhood Malibu mansion became a landmarkThe Carbon Canyon Estate, situated at 3903 Carbon Canyon Road in Malibu, was more than an impressive celebrity residence. It was the home where Gigi, Bella and their brother Anwar spent part of their childhood, making it closely connected to the Hadid family’s personal history.According to Realtor, Yolanda Hadid and musician David Foster purchased the property in 2007 for $4.5 million. The couple subsequently undertook renovations, transforming it into a substantial residence that reflected their lifestyle and family needs.The mansion also became familiar to television audiences through its appearances on The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills, in which Yolanda featured between 2012 and 2016. Its visibility on the programme helped establish the property as a recognisable part of the family's public life.Yolanda and Foster eventually sold the estate in 2015 for $19.5 million, two years before their divorce was finalised. The property subsequently changed hands, although its ownership at the time of the January 2025 wildfires was unclear.What made the estate stand out in MalibuThe mansion occupied a 3.25-acre site with views of the Pacific Ocean and the surrounding landscape. Its location, privacy and scale made it particularly attractive in Malibu, where properties with expansive grounds and ocean views command considerable attention.Realtor reported that the estate had 6 bedrooms and 11 bathrooms. Its earlier listing described the property as a private residence with views from multiple directions, presenting it as an example of high-end Malibu living.The home was also associated with Kylie Jenner, who reportedly rented it in 2019. Realtor reported its asking price at $34.99 million when the wildfires struck in January 2025.The estate's appeal was not limited to its size. It represented a combination of architectural character, coastal scenery and celebrity history, factors that had helped sustain its substantial valuation before the disaster.Bella Hadid shared the emotional loss of her childhood homeThe destruction of the mansion became particularly personal for Bella Hadid, who publicly acknowledged the loss through social media posts during the wildfires.The model later posted an aerial photograph showing the aftermath, with the building visibly charred and much of its structure destroyed.For Bella, the mansion represented years of family experiences, childhood memories and a place associated with growing up alongside her siblings.The loss also came amid a wider disaster affecting thousands of residents across Los Angeles. The January 2025 wildfires destroyed homes, displaced families and damaged entire neighbourhoods, including Malibu and Pacific Palisades.The Malibu property returned to the market as vacant landFollowing the destruction, the estate's value became closely tied to its land rather than the residence that had previously occupied it.Realtor reported that the property was relisted in May 2025 for $16 million, with Daniel Milstein and Aaron Kirman of Christie's International Real Estate Southern California representing the parcel.The listing presented the vacant site as an opportunity for a buyer to rebuild a substantial Malibu residence. Plans associated with the earlier property included a proposed 14,000-square-foot mansion featuring 6 bedrooms, 7 full bathrooms and three half-bathrooms.The designs also included a home theatre, gym, spa, games room and extensive outdoor entertainment facilities. Three swimming pools, a bocce court and a sports court were among the features envisioned for the estate.However, the property ultimately sold for considerably less than its post-fire asking price.A $6.5 million sale reflects Malibu's changing property marketAccording to Realtor, the 3.25-acre parcel eventually sold for $6.5 million, just over a year after the mansion was destroyed. The buyer's identity was not disclosed. The sale represented an important transaction in Malibu's property market, with the publication describing it as the area's most expensive land sale since the wildfires.Speaking to TMZ, listing agent Daniel Milstein said he and Kirman were proud of the sale and hoped it demonstrated the resilience of Malibu and the wider Los Angeles area.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 2 more executions set in Florida and Alabama, hours after lethal injection in Indiana
articles.summary: The death penalty has faced renewed scrutiny since the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee, although courts have rejected efforts to halt other executions after she survived two doses of pentobarbital.
articles.body: Florida and Alabama plan to execute two men Thursday for killing older adults during home robberies, just hours after Indiana put a prisoner to death in the first of three lethal injections scheduled for the same day in the U.S. It would be Florida’s 19th execution this year under Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis, matching a record set by the state in 2025, and the second time this year that three people would be put to death on the same day. The death penalty has faced renewed scrutiny since the September failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee, although courts have rejected efforts to halt other executions after she survived two doses of pentobarbital. In Indiana, Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, was pronounced dead at 12:45 a.m. at the state prison in Michigan City, said Noelle Russell, spokesperson at the Department of Correction. She said Weisheit’s final meal was barbecue ribs and he had no final words. He had acknowledged killing his girlfriend's two children in a house fire in the Evansville area in 2010 but had hoped that Gov. Mike Braun would grant clemency and change his sentence to life in prison. Braun declined. In Indiana, lawyers failed to persuade Braun, a Republican, to allow Weisheit to undergo brain scans in an effort to reinforce their argument that he has a history of head injuries and mental health problems that should foreclose execution. Weisheit's last objection centered on the state's planned use of lethal drugs purchased from a pharmacy that is facing a disciplinary hearing next week at the Indiana Pharmacy Board. The Indiana Supreme Court declined to intervene Wednesday night, though two of the five justices wanted a 10-day stay for more information about the drugs' expiration and storage. The execution provided “long-awaited justice for Alyssa Lynch and her brother Caleb, two innocent children whose lives were stolen in an act of unspeakable cruelty," Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita said.

articles.title: Met Police 'reset' means fewer officers at events and protests
articles.summary: Sir Mark Rowley says police officers are being moved to boost community policing.
articles.body:
A "resetting" of policing priorities in London will mean that some incidents at major events and protests will now "take longer to squash", the Metropolitan Police has said.

Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley told a session of the London Assembly that officers were being moved away from policing major events and into community policing instead.

The decision, he said, freed up 6,000 shifts in October.

The commissioner asked the Assembly for "support" in making the changes, which he said were due to "financial pressures".

Sir Mark said to Assembly members: "London's politicians, including yourselves, regularly say to me, 'My local neighbourhood officers are great, but you abstract them too much.'

"So this is about reducing that, but it does come with a challenge.

"It will mean that sometimes events in the centre of London will happen in a way that wasn't anticipated, and will take longer to squash and deal with.

"So I would ask for your support when that happens because the prize for taking that more measured approach is that we have more resources in local communities."

Sir Mark also told the Assembly that the force was facing "challenges" with the volume of misconduct cases involving its officers, which had "massively increased" in recent years.

The commissioner described the threshold to investigate issues as "so low".

He explained that officers' time was being consumed "investigating trivial matters".

It comes after Susan Hall, leader of the Conservatives on the Assembly, said that during a recent committee meeting they were "told by the Met Fed (Metropolitan Police Federation) that thousands of officers are on restricted duties or even garden leave, waiting for their investigation for misconduct to be heard".

Sir Mark agreed that misconduct cases had been taking "too long", but said in the past six months "the number of days per case is going down rapidly".

He added: "There is currently a review of the system commissioned by the home secretary.

"I'm concerned that the police regulations don't give enough discretion on which cases to investigate and which cases to not."

articles.title: Iraq airspace available again, Air India flights between Delhi, Mumbai and New York become nonstop; shave 4 hours off from Rome one-stops
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a “Diwali gift” to travellers, Air India has once again made its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York (JFK and Newark EWR) nonstop
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a “Diwali gift” to travellers, Air India has once again made its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York (JFK and Newark EWR) nonstop since Wednesday, shaving close to four hours from the travel time of the one-stops these had become since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb 28. The airline's operations team, like that of other carriers, does constantly analyses enroute geopolitical situation and as soon as the risk rating for Iraq, Syria and Jordan reduced, it has started got a slightly shorter route available making the flights between Delhi and EWR; Delhi and JFK; Mumbai and EWR and Mumbai and JFK nonstop once again, skipping the Rome Fiumicino stop. Now the journeys become 15-16 hours, instead of the almost 20 hours they took with the Rome stop.The closure of Pakistan airspace since last April had made routes longer between Delhi and the west but the Iran airspace was open till Feb 28 when the US-Iran war broke out. Since then, the non-availability of Iran, Iraq and other enroute airspaces forced fuelling stops to be added. Now while Iran remains out of bounds, the Iraq airspace has become available and AI flight operations has seized the opportunity to make the New York flights nonstops again.While no one knows when and if Pakistan airspace will reopen for Indian carriers, AI is hoping that Iran airspace opens so that it can add more nonstops to the west. As of now in the current situation, its flights between Delhi/Mumbai and New York are likely to remain nonstop in Nov and Dec. From Jan, the winds become very strong and if the loads are high then fuelling stops may return for some time.“There is load penalty (restriction in number of passengers and/or cargo to carry more fuel for longer routes) since Pakistan airspace closed. So that remains. What has changed for now is that Iraq has become available again and made the flights nonstops again,” said pilots who operate this route.With the devastating economic impact of the US-Iran war on the midterms and Republicans facing a rout there, there is hope that the war will come to an end. If that happens, AI will add much more capacity to the west, including North America.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Valley recruitment stopped this year: Police chiefSRINAGAR: Kashmir has just one active local terrorist and recruitment in the valley completely stopped this year, while security forces were tracking a handful of foreign terrorists believed to be assisting him, J&K police IG Sujit Kumar said Thursday.Police identified the lone local terrorist as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district. articles.title: Jen Lilley is bringing back the ‘Christmas Is Not Cancelled’ toy drive she started during the COVID-19 pandemic, with a goal of 20,000 presents and a $30,000 donation from Shawn Ryan
articles.summary: On Christmas Eve, most kids wake up, skip breakfast, run down the hall and look under the tree for the gifts Santa left behind.
articles.body: On Christmas Eve, most kids wake up, skip breakfast, run down the hall and look under the tree for the gifts Santa left behind. For most of them, the wrapping paper is there. For some, it isn’t, and the morning goes quiet in a way no parent forgets. Not every parent can afford a present, and actress Jen Lilley, who is a mum of five, understands what that means. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she started the Christmas Is Not Cancelled toy drive, which has turned into something much bigger than she expected. Her goal this year is to provide 20,000 presents for children in need, and the campaign is backed by a $30,000 donation from podcaster Shawn Ryan towards bikes and scooters, items Lilley says are often the hardest to source. The campaign kicked off on 1 November and will run through 13 December, People reported.The campaign started as a jokeThe idea started almost by accident. During the pandemic, Lilley told a friend that Christmas had better not get cancelled, then realised that for plenty of families, it might be. The organisation began “as a joke during the pandemic”, Lilley told the outlet. “I told a girlfriend, ‘They’d better not cancel Christmas,’ and then it hit me that for so many families, it actually might be. As a mum of five and a child advocate, I couldn’t stand the thought of a child waking up on Christmas morning to nothing and wondering if they’d landed on the naughty list,” she recalled.The initial goal was to provide 10,000 presents for children in need. The campaign set out to achieve a single goal: no child should have to wonder whether they had landed on the naughty list. The campaign was undoubtedly a success. The drive grew steadily through 2021, 2022 and 2023, eventually distributing around 25,000 toys and books each Christmas.“What I never expected was how much it would mean, not just to the recipients, but to the people giving. So many of us felt like what we had to offer wasn’t enough to make a difference. But it was! Sure, most people couldn’t give $1,000, but a lot of people could give $15 for a book. But they didn’t just give a book! They joined thousands of strangers from all across the country, and together, those books and toys added up to more than 10,000 presents.” The campaign then paused for two years.Reviving the campaignLilley is now reviving the campaign, with a target of 20,000 presents. “I honestly haven’t stopped smiling. Bringing Christmas Is Not Cancelled back feels like my own Christmas miracle,” the actress told the outlet, expressing her excitement about the revival. This year, there is one structural change. The programme is now a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, which makes donations tax-deductible.Podcaster Shawn Ryan has also joined the effort, committing $30,000 towards bikes and scooters. “When I went on Shawn’s show to talk about foster care, he really listened. Now he’s turning that conversation into action. I can’t tell you everything I got for Christmas growing up, but I’ll never forget the year I got a bike. Now, thanks to Shawn, kids who’ve spent Christmas wondering if anyone remembered them will wake up to a bike with their name on it,” the actress revealed.The campaign works with Toys for Tots. But here’s the best part: parents get to choose the gifts themselves, so on Christmas morning, the presents arrive from Mum and Dad! “No parent wants to tell their child they couldn’t afford Christmas,” Lilley said. The arrangement allows parents to retain their dignity while their children continue believing everything is fine.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: How to stop your pipes from freezing this winter, according to plumbers
articles.summary: Frozen pipes can burst and cause costly water damage. Plumbers share how to keep your pipes from freezing and what to do if one bursts.
articles.body: Nothing ruins a winter morning quite like turning on the faucet and getting nothing but a sputter, or worse, finding water pouring through your ceiling. When temperatures plunge, the water inside your pipes can freeze and expand, putting enough pressure on them to crack or even burst. The result is water damage, a hefty repair bill and a big headache. The good news is that frozen pipes are largely preventable, and most of the fixes are cheap, quick and easy enough to handle yourself. To find out how to keep the water flowing all winter, I spoke to two plumbing experts about how frozen pipes happen, what you can do to protect yours before the next cold snap and how to handle the situation if your pipes do freeze. What causes pipes to freeze? Pipes freeze when the water inside them gets cold enough to turn to ice — and some parts of your plumbing are far more vulnerable than others. “Pipes can freeze when they’re exposed to cold temperatures without enough insulation or heat to protect them,” says Steve Clemente, president and COO at Benjamin Franklin Plumbing. “This is especially a concern for outdoor plumbing and pipes that run through unheated areas of the home, like an attic or basement.” The real danger isn’t the ice itself but rather what happens when water freezes. “As water freezes, it expands,” says Mike Rippel, owner of Quality Pro Services, a plumbing and heating company in Middlesex, New Jersey. And according to Clemente, “a frozen pipe can burst, leaving you with water damage and potentially costly repairs.” The first sign of a frozen pipe is usually a faucet that won’t run, or only trickles, when you turn it on. You might also notice frost on exposed pipes or hear unusual sounds when water tries to move through them. A frozen pipe isn’t always a disaster, but it’s a warning sign you shouldn’t ignore. What can help you prevent frozen pipes? To find out which products are worth considering, I asked Clemente and Rippel what they recommend homeowners use to protect their pipes from freezing. Here are the types of products they suggested. Clemente says heat tape can help protect pipes and keep them from freezing. This tape wraps pipes, valves and fittings to reduce heat loss and gain in plumbing and air-conditioning systems. Its pressure-sensitive adhesive backing installs quickly without fasteners, and the foam is mold-resistant. If you’d prefer not to wrap tape around your pipes, Rippel says foam pipe covers also work to help prevent freezing. A pack of these from Duck holds six pre-slit, 1-foot black sticks (6 ft. total) with self-sealing adhesive edges for easy installation. They fit half-inch to three-quarter-inch pipes, can be trimmed to fit the length of your pipe and can easily be removed once winter is over. These outdoor faucet covers slip over spigots to help shield them from winter frost and freezing temperatures. Each cover has a polyester shell, a thick layer of insulating cotton and a long drawstring strap that cinches it shut. Reflective strips make the covers easy to spot in the dark so you don’t bang into it if you’re walking outside. “Smart sensors can provide another layer of protection by detecting drastic temperature changes or water where it shouldn’t be,” says Clemente. This one attaches to your main water supply pipe and tracks the temperature of the water inside. If the water gets cold enough to put your pipes at risk, it can automatically shut off your water supply and send an alert to your phone. It also monitors water flow to flag leaks. You can install it yourself, though Moen recommends hiring a professional. Other things you can do to prevent frozen pipes Beyond buying products that can help prevent your pipes from freezing, experts say there are a few other things you can do to mitigate the risk. Prep your outdoor plumbing. “Start before cold weather arrives by disconnecting garden hoses or other faucets and draining outdoor water lines you won’t use during the winter,” says Clemente.Insulate exposed pipes. “Insulate exposed pipes, especially those outdoors or in unheated spaces like attics and basements,” says Clemente.Keep the heat on. “Have your heating system serviced, and keep the heat on low even when you’re away so the temperature inside your home doesn’t drop too low,” says Clemente.Let your faucets drip. During especially cold nights, “run the faucet at a slow but steady drip to prevent the water from freezing,” says Rippel. How cold does it need to be for your pipes to freeze? “Exposure to temperatures below 32 degrees [Fahrenheit} can cause pipes to freeze and potentially burst,” says Clementes. But pipes don’t necessarily freeze the moment temperatures dip below that mark. How quickly it happens depends on how cold it gets, how long the cold lasts and how well your pipes are protected. “Pipes outdoors or in unheated, poorly insulated areas are particularly vulnerable because they stay cold for longer, so protect those lines before freezing weather arrives,” says Clemente. How can you tell if your pipes are frozen? If water freezes and expands in your pipes it can cause cracks or even cause the pipe to burst. And because the water is frozen, the leak may not start until the ice thaws and water begins flowing through the damaged section again, says Rippel. If a pipe does burst, where that pipe is located may determine how much damage you have to deal with. Depending on the location, that water can soak into drywall, flooring and insulation before you even realize there’s a leak, which is why it’s important to act quickly if you suspect a pipe has frozen. What should you do if a pipe does burst? The most important thing is to stop the flow of water as quickly as possible. “Shut down the incoming water system so that when the line does thaw, you don’t have consistent running water causing major flooding,” says Rippel. This is why it pays to plan ahead. “It’s also a good idea to know where your main water shutoff valve is and make sure it works so you’re prepared if a pipe does burst,” says Clemente. Once the water is off, call a licensed plumber to assess and repair the damaged pipe. If water is near outlets, appliances or your electrical panel, turn off power to the affected area before you start cleaning up. It’s also a good idea to take photos of the damage and contact your homeowners insurance company, since many policies cover sudden water damage from a burst pipe. Want more from NBC Selected? We also ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Steve Clemente is the president and COO at Benjamin Franklin Plumbing. Mike Rippel is the owner of Quality Pro Services, a plumbing and heating company in Middlesex, New Jersey. articles.title: Travelers busted at airport with over 3,000 tarantulas hidden away in their socks
articles.summary: Over 3,000 tarantulas were found hidden inside pairs of socks in three suitcases at a Peru airport, leading to the detention of two Germans and one Polish citizen.
articles.body: More than 3,000 tarantulas were discovered stuffed inside socks that were packed in the luggage of three different travelers as they prepared to board a flight. The spiders were found Nov. 3 in three suitcases at an airport in Callao, Peru, according to Reuters. The luggage belonged to two German citizens and one Polish citizen who were preparing to fly to Germany, according to SERFOR, Peru's National Forestry and Wildlife Service. MAN BUSTED AFTER CUSTOMS UNCOVERS BIZARRE CARGO HIDDEN INSIDE 22 PAIRS OF SOCKS Authorities launched an investigation after receiving an anonymous tip. When officials searched the suitcases, they found between 15 and 22 socks packed inside each one, concealing spiders of different species and in varying numbers, Reuters reported. The seizure included tarantulas at different stages of development, from eggs and young spiders to adults. Cora Suarez, a wildlife forestry control technician with SERFOR, said the creatures can be valuable to collectors. "These species are attractive because of the colors, because of the size and, more than anything, because they can be intended for collectors," Suarez said in Spanish. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The three travelers were stopped while checking in for their flight. They were detained by Peru's environmental crimes police, according to Reuters. Authorities said the travelers now face criminal proceedings led by a specialized environmental prosecutor's office. Keith Jeffries, an Orlando-based vice president of K2 Security Screening Group and former federal security director at Los Angeles International Airport, previously told Fox News Digital that money can drive unusual wildlife smuggling attempts. "If there's a market for it, people will attempt to smuggle it," Jeffries said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES "We've seen this before many times," he added. "It happens more frequently than any of us would like." Jeffries said airport screening responsibilities can vary depending on the agency and what officers are tasked with finding. In the U.S., for example, Transportation Security Administration officers primarily search for aviation security threats such as weapons and explosives rather than specifically looking for smuggled wildlife, he said. The tarantula discovery is not the first time authorities have found living creatures hidden inside socks in travelers' luggage. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ In August, a 23-year-old man was arrested at Tokyo's Haneda Airport after authorities discovered about 200 lizards packed inside 22 pairs of socks in his suitcase, Fox News Digital previously reported. Nine of the reptiles were Mexican alligator lizards, an endangered species subject to international trade restrictions. Some could reportedly sell for hundreds of dollars each in Japan. articles.title: Paraguay president Santiago Peña resigns amid Ueno Bank collapse, faces impeachment
articles.summary: Paraguayan president Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday after the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank triggered widespread protests, froze millions of
articles.body: Paraguayan president Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday after the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank triggered widespread protests, froze millions of dollars in deposits and cost him the backing of his ruling Colorado Party. Minutes after his announcement, the country's lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, sending the charges to the Senate.According to The Associated Press (AP), congressional leaders were expected to accept Peña's resignation later on Thursday, potentially clearing the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to take office without waiting for a Senate trial.Announcing his decision in a video posted on X, Peña said he was stepping down in the interest of “the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions.”“I want to apologize to the people if I have failed them at any point,” he said. “It was never my intention to betray the trust they placed in me."The resignation came after Peña lost the support of his political mentor, former President and Colorado Party leader Horacio Cartes, who backed impeachment proceedings.Cartes said the party would not side with “the plundering of public and private funds and pensioners’ money”. The US Treasury had sanctioned Cartes in 2023 over bribery allegations, which the Trump administration lifted last year.Ueno Bank collapse: What triggered the political crisis?Ueno Bank, which expanded rapidly from a relatively obscure financial company into one of Paraguay's most prominent digital lenders, had more than three million customers, representing a significant share of the country's 6.5 million population, according to company figures.The bank's expansion came under scrutiny over alleged risky lending to companies linked to its controlling shareholder, Grupo Vázquez. Paraguay's central bank reportedly identified loans to related companies that exceeded legal limits and lacked adequate collateral.The regulator intervened after finding poorly documented loans and expenses incorrectly counted as assets. Following corrections to its accounts, Ueno's capital fell below half the legally required minimum, prompting the central bank to seize the lender and initiate resolution proceedings.The bank had reported holding approximately $800 million in public deposits, including funds belonging to state institutions, pension-related bodies and operators of the country's hydroelectric dams.Peña had previously held a stake in a company linked to Grupo Vázquez but said he sold it in March 2025. He had also appointed Carlos Carvallo, former head of Financiera Ueno, the bank's predecessor, as central bank chief. Carvallo resigned after the intervention.Meanwhile, prosecutors charged 27 bank officials and associates with breach of trust and attempted fraud. A judge ordered six executives, including founder Miguel Vázquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale, jailed pending trial.The collapse left customers unable to access savings through the bank's application, cards and branches. Authorities have introduced a state-backed deposit guarantee mechanism to reimburse eligible customers, with payments beginning with smaller accounts.Protests continued after Peña's resignation, with employees demanding unpaid wages and depositors seeking accountability. The Labour Ministry estimated that around 7,000 direct and indirect jobs were affected.Under Paraguay's Constitution, former presidents become senators for life and receive parliamentary immunity unless removed through impeachment. The proceedings against Peña could therefore have significant implications beyond his departure from office.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A British family doctor was convicted of murdering 15 patients; a public inquiry later concluded that Harold Shipman had killed at least 215, exposing how a trusted physician evaded suspicion for years
articles.summary: A doctor with an injection is there to protect you.
articles.body: A doctor with an injection is there to protect you. But what happens if the injection turns lethal in the same hands of a doctor, and no less than someone trusted enough to be your family doctor. For more than 200 patients, what began as an ordinary consultation with a trusted family doctor would end in a horrifying crime. Harold Shipman, a general practitioner who worked in England for nearly three decades, was convicted of murdering 15 patients in 2000. But as investigations progressed, what was revealed was far too ghastly: Shipman was found to have been responsible for the deaths of at least 215 of his patients, with the final public inquiry estimating that the figure could have been around 250.To his regular patients, Shipman was not a face you forget, but in fact a face that you like. As a family doctor, he had access to the patients' homes, where he was often called upon to treat elderly people and made medical judgements that were rarely ever questioned at the time.Shipman was not an unfamiliar face to the people who visited his surgery. As a family doctor, he had access to patients in their homes, was often called upon to treat elderly people and was in a position where his medical judgement was rarely questioned. It was this trust, combined with his ability to make deaths appear medically unremarkable, that allowed him to continue killing patients without attracting sufficient attention for years.His crimes stretched across several medical practices, beginning in Todmorden, West Yorkshire, where he worked after qualifying as a doctor, and continuing in Hyde, Greater Manchester, the final location of his crimes. According to the first report of the Shipman Inquiry, chaired by High Court judge Dame Janet Smith, the first reported victim dates back to 1975 with the killings having continued until June 1998. His victims were predominantly elderly women, although men and younger patients were also among those he killed.The inquiry established that his usual method involved administering a lethal dose of an opiate, most frequently diamorphine, a drug also known as heroin that has medical uses as a powerful painkiller. In many cases, the deaths appeared to be natural, making it difficult for families and authorities to recognise a pattern. The fact that Shipman was a practising doctor also meant that his presence at the time of death was not, by itself, considered unusual.However, it was the death of an 81 year-old woman, Kathleen Grundy, that eventually caused suspicion. Grundy, a former mayor of Hyde, was found dead at her home on June 24, 1998. Her daughter, Angela Woodruff, a solicitor, became suspicious when she discovered a will supposedly made by her mother, which named Shipman as the sole beneficiary of her estate. But Woodruff believed the document was forged and first reported it to the police.What initially appeared to be a case of possible fraud soon developed into a murder investigation. Grundy's body was exhumed, and forensic examination revealed the presence of morphine in her tissues. Shipman was arrested in September 1998, and investigators began examining the deaths of other patients who had died unexpectedly while under his care. Eventually, 15 murders, including Grundy's, were selected for prosecution. On January 31, 2000, Shipman was found guilty of all 15 murders and of forging Grundy's will.The conviction, however, was only the beginning of understanding the scale of what had happened. In 2001, the government established the Shipman Inquiry to investigate the extent of his crimes and examine how he had managed to evade detection. Its first report, published in July 2002, concluded that he had killed at least 215 patients. Another 45 deaths raised what the inquiry described as a real suspicion of further murders, although there was insufficient evidence to reach a definite conclusion.A report published in the British Medical Journal on July 27, 2002, by journalist Owen Dyer, documented the findings and noted that the inquiry had examined 888 cases. Of these, 215 were determined to be murders committed by Shipman. The investigation also found that 171 of his confirmed victims were women and 44 were men. The inquiry's sixth and final report, published in January 2005, subsequently extended its examination to his earlier career as a junior doctor at Pontefract General Infirmary. Dame Janet Smith ultimately estimated that Shipman had killed approximately 250 patients over the course of his medical career.Perhaps one of the most troubling aspects of the case was that there had been an opportunity to stop Shipman before his arrest. In March 1998, Dr Linda Reynolds, a doctor working at a neighbouring practice, raised concerns with the local coroner about the unusually high number of deaths among Shipman's patients and the circumstances surrounding them. Greater Manchester Police investigated the matter, but the inquiry later found serious shortcomings in the way it was handled. The investigation was closed in April without uncovering evidence of wrongdoing. Shipman went on to kill three more patients before his arrest five months later. The second Shipman Inquiry report, published on July 14, 2003, concluded that those deaths would probably have been prevented had the earlier investigation been properly conducted and supervised.The inquiry therefore went only to examine not only Shipman's actions but also the institutions that had failed to recognise the warning signs, the false note keeping of the patient records and the issuance of death certificates and a major one being the permissions granted for cremation.Through this questioning, procedures for certifying deaths, the role of coroners, the monitoring of controlled drugs and the handling of complaints against doctors all came under scrutiny. It became clear that the problem was not simply that one individual had committed an extraordinary number of murders, but that several safeguards designed to protect patients had failed to work as intended.Shipman was serving a life sentence when he was found dead in his prison cell at Wakefield Prison on January 13, 2004. His death was ruled a suicide. He continued to maintain his innocence, and the full explanation for why he killed so many of his patients has till date remained unknown, where even the inquiry led by Dame Janet Smith could not determine the exact motive.The Shipman case remains one of Britain's most disturbing criminal investigations, not only because of the number of lives lost but the circumstances in which the very image of treatment was inverted to look like the image of a monstrous death. With some research inquiries wondering if Shipman was addicted to the act of killing itself may have been plausible, but having rejected any kind of psychiatric report, all that is left is conjecture: a fact that many lost their lives in the hands of those who they must've wished to have saved them. At last, a question remains: for how long can professional medical authority go unquestioned, and why did years of oversight culminate in devastating consequences?You use AI every day. articles.title: A Pennsylvania couple fought to make their town maintain public steps that cross their private land; after evidence of 130 years of public use and repairs, an appeals court upheld the borough's duty to maintain them
articles.summary: Public steps connecting two streets may look like an ordinary part of a neighbourhood, but responsibility for maintaining them can become complicated when
articles.body: Public steps connecting two streets may look like an ordinary part of a neighbourhood, but responsibility for maintaining them can become complicated when they run across privately owned land. A Pennsylvania couple faced that issue after their borough disputed its obligation to maintain a set of steps that had been used by residents for generations. The couple argued that the public had relied on the passage for more than a century and that the borough had repeatedly repaired and maintained it using public resources.The dispute reached Pennsylvania's Commonwealth Court after the Borough of Jim Thorpe challenged a lower court ruling requiring it to continue maintaining the High Street Steps. In its October 30, 2026, decision in TM Loughery and MK Loughery v. Borough of Jim Thorpe, docket number 466 C.D. 2025, available on Justia, the appeals court upheld the ruling. It found that 130 years of uninterrupted public use, together with historical evidence of the borough's involvement in repairs and reconstruction, established that the steps had been dedicated to public use and accepted by the borough.Couple challenged borough's responsibility for the stepsThomas M Loughery and Michelle K Loughery owned a property at 49 West Broadway in Jim Thorpe, Carbon County, Pennsylvania. The High Street Steps connected two public roads, High Street and West Broadway, allowing people to walk between them without passing through private locations. However, the steps were situated partly on the couple's property, partly on an adjoining property owned by 61 West Broadway LLC, and partly on land owned by the borough along High Street.The couple alleged that the borough had previously maintained and repaired the steps but later denied responsibility for them. On February 14, 2019, they filed a lawsuit seeking a declaration that the borough owned the steps. They also argued that the passage had been dedicated to public use through its long history of unrestricted access.The trial court held a non-jury trial on May 11, 2023, and on June 3, 2024, found in the couple's favour on their dedication claim. It ruled in the borough's favour on their separate ejectment claim. After the trial court denied its post-trial motion in December 2024, the borough appealed on January 7, 2025. The trial court subsequently entered formal judgment in favour of the couple on September 25, 2026.130 years of public use supported the dedication claimThe borough argued that there was no formal record showing that its council had accepted the steps through an ordinance or resolution. It also described its historical maintenance activities as limited, arguing that occasional repairs over 130 years were insufficient to establish responsibility. The couple countered that residents had freely and continuously used the steps for more than a century. They also presented evidence that the borough had spent public money constructing, rebuilding and repairing the passage.The Commonwealth Court explained that Pennsylvania law recognises both express and implied dedication of property for public use. An implied dedication can be established through a series of actions demonstrating an intention to make property available for public purposes. The judges also referred to earlier legal decisions establishing that prolonged public use and municipal actions can demonstrate acceptance even without a formal resolution.The court found that the public's uninterrupted use of the High Street Steps for 130 years established a conclusive presumption of the owners' dedication and the borough's acceptance. It also noted that the borough council's own records provided evidence of its involvement.Historical records documented the borough's involvement with the stepsOne of the important parts of the case was the evidence from historical borough council meeting minutes. Records from August 6, 1912, showed that a council member had suggested inspecting the steps and deciding how to make them more substantial and permanent. Minutes from September 3, 1912, recorded instructions to have them paved with substantial material. The borough's involvement continued decades later. In November 1977, officials obtained a repair estimate, while the borough's 1978 budget included $8,000 for reconstruction of the High Street Steps.In August 1978, the council also authorised advertising for bids to repair the passage. A September 2014 letter sent by the borough to residents further acknowledged the need to replace the steps. The appeals court considered these records evidence of authorised or ratified municipal actions. Together with the long history of public use, they supported the conclusion that the borough had accepted the dedication.Appeals court upheld borough's maintenance obligationThe borough also argued that it had the authority to decide whether the steps should remain open and how much maintenance they required under the Pennsylvania Borough Code. However, the appeals court explained that the borough's responsibility did not arise from a formal statutory dedication under the code. Instead, it resulted from a common-law dedication established through public use and the borough's actions.The court also discussed Pennsylvania's Donated or Dedicated Property Act, which treats dedicated public property as being held by a municipality in trust for the benefit of the public. This means the municipality has responsibilities towards property dedicated to public use. Referring to earlier decisions, the judges explained that a municipality has a legal duty to keep dedicated public passages in reasonably safe condition for public travel.Ultimately, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court affirmed the lower court's ruling, leaving the Borough of Jim Thorpe responsible for continuing to maintain the High Street Steps. The decision established that the absence of a formal acceptance document did not excuse the borough from its obligations when more than a century of public use and historical municipal records demonstrated its acceptance of the passage.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Speedy trial is a fundamental right’: SC says Constitution has primacy over special laws
articles.summary: 'Speedy trial is a fundamental right, can't tinker' NEW DELHI: The Constitution will prevail over all other laws and regulations, Supreme Court said on
articles.body: 'Speedy trial is a fundamental right, can't tinker'NEW DELHI: The Constitution will prevail over all other laws and regulations, Supreme Court said on Thursday and made it clear that in case of any contradiction or conflict between constitutional provisions and special laws like NDPS, UAPA and PMLA, it is the former which will triumph.It reiterated that the right to speedy trial was a fundamental right and could not be violated under any law and could be the ground for bail.The bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar faulted the apex court's earlier order, which held that under special statutes such as NDPS Act, an accused's right under Article 21 (speedy trial) must be exercised within the confines of Section 37 of the Act (stringent bail conditions) and cannot be invoked solely on the ground of prolonged delay to override Section 37.The latest ruling comes amid sharp differences within the apex court over granting bail in PMLA, NDPS and UAPA cases on grounds of delay in trial, with the issue now before a larger bench.SC: Constitution should be guide to interpret law, not the other way roundJustices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar also said fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes.The bench said, "First and foremost, the rights conferred by Article 21 of the Constitution are not only constitutional rights. These are fundamental rights. Right to life and liberty as enshrined in Article 21 are at the core of our constitutional jurisprudence. These fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under the special statutes."Such observations run counter to numerous judgements of this court which reiterate the proposition that when there is a violation of Article 21 of the Constitution, the rigour of Section 37 of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act or similar such provisions under special statutes would have to give way, the court said.The court's observation assumes significance as there are differences of opinion within Supreme Court on the issue of bail in offences under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), NDPS and Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) on grounds of delay in trial. Contradictory orders have been passed on whether the fundamental right to have a speedy trial would prevail over stringent bail conditions stipulated under special laws, with one bench saying the right to speedy trial cannot be the ground to grant bail in PMLA, UAPA offences while other benches took contradictory stands.The controversy now stands referred to a larger bench after two benches took swipes at each other in their judicial orders. "A statute, special or otherwise, cannot be a guide to interpret the Constitution; rather, it should be the other way round. To reiterate, a fundamental right must be interpreted in such a manner that it upholds and furthers the objective of such a fundamental right," the bench said, adding, "The court must interpret the Constitution in a manner which would enable citizens to enjoy the rights guaranteed by it in the fullest measure."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Escaped Tennessee killer hid in Illinois shed with beer and garlic bread before capture: Sheriff
articles.summary: Jacob Allen Morley hid in an Illinois shed near Marion, drinking beer and making garlic bread before FLOCK cameras helped track the Tennessee escapee.
articles.body: A convicted killer who broke out of a Tennessee prison spent his time on the run hiding in a shed, drinking beer and making garlic bread, officials said. Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, on Oct. 25 and was recaptured by authorities on Tuesday. He was arrested without incident after authorities used FLOCK cameras to help track him down, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol. "On November 3, 2026, at approximately 9:30 a.m., the Patrol’s Missouri Information Analysis Center and Troop A Communications received information from the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation that Morley may be traveling westbound on Interstate 70 near Independence," the Missouri State Highway Patrol said in a statement. "The suspect vehicle was located using FLOCK cameras, and officers began to deploy to the area. With additional use of FLOCK cameras, the suspect vehicle was located by undercover officers traveling south on Missouri 291 in Liberty." FLOCK EXECUTIVE DEFENDS CRIME-FIGHTING CAMERAS AS ACLU ATTORNEY QUESTIONS COMPANY'S MOTIVES AMID BACKLASH Investigators believe Morley sheltered for a period in a shed near Marion, Illinois, that hunters used on an occasional basis, roughly 127 miles from the prison he escaped. Williamson County Sheriff Jeff Diederich said evidence indicates Morley consumed beer and prepared garlic bread along with other food during his time there. Morley also wrote a handwritten letter of apology after taking a truck from the farm, Diederich said. He allegedly took clothes and three firearms from the property as well. TENNESSEE PRISON CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER FAILED EXECUTION AS FORMER US ATTORNEY TAPPED TO LEAD INDEPENDENT REVIEW The Illinois sheriff said he believes Morley covered roughly three miles on foot after leaving behind a separate truck he had used following the prison escape. "How he ended up in Marion is kind of a mystery," Diederich said. articles.title: ‘I guess I’m dead’: Tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson's chilling post resurfaces after he, wife and two young children die in Florida plane crash
articles.summary: A social media post made 3 years ago has recently taken on an unsettling meaning after resurfacing online.
articles.body: A social media post made 3 years ago has recently taken on an unsettling meaning after resurfacing online. Adam Robinson, 45, a tech entrepreneur who was killed along with his wife, two young children and five others in a private plane crash in Florida, had once replied to an online discussion with the words, “I guess I'm dead” on X. A seemingly sarcastic remark made during a conversation about the tech startup industry has now resurfaced following his death in the fatal accident on Sunday, November 1, 2026, drawing attention from users who have revisited his old posts.Robinson's post dates back to July 19, 2023, when he was engaging in a conversation on Twitter, now known as X, about where software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies should be built. The discussion involved a suggestion that some of the best technology companies were being built in Tel Aviv. Robinson responded with the brief remark, “I guess I'm dead.” At the time, the tweet was understood as a sarcastic response to the conversation rather than anything more serious. However, following news of his death, the words began circulating again, with people pointing out the coincidence between the old remark and the circumstances in which he lost his life.The post attracted renewed attention after Robinson was identified among the nine people killed when a Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, on November 1. According to the Federal Aviation Administration, the flight was headed to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas when the crash killed everyone on board.The passengers included Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp, their children Emma and Charlie, family nanny Anita Maria Cetina, and family friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr. The children were four and two years old, respectively. Their deaths were confirmed in a joint statement released by the families, which described Adam and Helen as devoted parents and remembered the warmth and generosity with which they welcomed people into their lives. The loss of the family, along with their friends and the two crew members, has also drawn attention from the technology community, where Robinson was known for his work as an entrepreneur.Robinson was the founder and CEO of Retention.com, RB2B as well as Moltsets, companies working in the marketing technology and website visitor identification space. Their products helped businesses identify people visiting their websites, allowing companies to better understand their audiences and connect with potential customers. He also founded MoltSets, an API-only business-to-business contact data platform. According to Inc., Robinson had built Retention.com into a company that generated $20 million in annual recurring revenue within 44 months, a milestone he had shared on LinkedIn.According to recordings of communications between the cockpit and air traffic control, as reported by Reuters, the crew had reported encountering light clear icing and moderate turbulence shortly before declaring an emergency. The pilots initially described the icing as manageable. The aircraft subsequently began a rapid descent, with the crew reporting an overspeed condition before issuing a mayday call. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash, with the cause yet to be established.You use AI every day. articles.title: Will Nigeria's Atiku Abubakar be on the presidential ballot after ADC court ruling?
articles.summary: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.
articles.body:
Nigeria's Federal High Court has sacked the leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) party - and also ruled that the nomination of its presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, is invalid.

A statement from the ADC said the ruling was another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition.

Presidential elections are scheduled to take place on 16 January when President Bola Tinubu's main challengers are again expected to be Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi.

Several high-profile politicians joined the ADC in 2025 - disillusioned by the factional infighting in the once powerful Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Amongst them were Abubakar - who had served as vice-president between 1999 and 2007 when the PDP was in power - and former Senate president David Mark.

As accommodations were made for the line-up of political heavy-weights, Mark took over as its interim chairman.

But Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former ADC national deputy chairman, argued before the court that this was not lawful as Mark and others had not been elected at a national convention.

Instead, he said, he himself should have taken over the party's leadership following the resignation of the ADC's former chairman in 2025.

Interestingly, this is not first time the Federal High Court in the capital, Abuja, has ruled on the leadership of the party.

In July, judge Musa Liman said Mark had been chosen in accordance with the country's laws and the party's constitution - in a case brought by another former ADC member.

Abubakar said the latest case raised serious legal concerns: "Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute?"

In a statement, the ADC added that Thursday's judgement by Justice Peter Lifu was aimed at stifling the opposition momentum and "was a calculated attempt to weaken the ADC and frustrate" Abubakar's candidacy.

The ADC says it will challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal.

He said the timing of the judgment was telling as it came "barely a day after a mammoth crowd turned out in Sokoto [northern Nigeria] to welcome him" at the launch of his campaign.

"The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning."

Political parties in Nigeria have increasingly been taking internal issues to court.

But as it stands, the electoral commission has issued its final list of candidates - and Abubakar is on the ticket for the ADC with former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as his running mate.

Will the latest ruling affect the opposition?

The ADC is effectively the most powerful opposition to President Tinubu. Many influential politicians opposed to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) have already defected to the party.

The legal saga could complicate things - it may cause uncertainty for hundreds of ADC candidates as well as raise questions over who has the authority to represent them.

But Abubakar, who hopes it will be seventh-time lucky in his ambition to be Nigeria's next president, is confident the matter will be resolved and called on his supporters not to be distracted.

"Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis. We urge our supporters to remain resolute, take our message from house to house and door to door, and stay peaceful and focused," the 79-year-old said.

Peter Obi - the other main presidential candidate who is on the ballot for a second time - has said he is shocked by Thursday's high court ruling.

He released a statement on X with the heading : "Do not undermine democracy".

The 65-year-old went on to say: "My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty.

Obi had briefly joined the ADC before leaving earlier this year to join the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) - in part because of the legal challenges within the ADC.

"The sustenance of democracy in Nigeria, in the midst of encroaching military rule in West Africa, should strengthen our resolve to protect opposition politics and not stamp out opposition parties," he said.

The NDC's candidate said that, as president, he would ensure that the existence of opposition parties would be respected.

"This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive."

Additional reporting by Chris Ewokor in Abuja

articles.title: Luke Bryan began taking his concerts to working farms in 2009; by the end of his 2026 Farm Tour, the project had awarded 97 college scholarships, while a sponsor-linked campaign had provided over 11 million meals
articles.summary: Luke Bryan began taking his concerts to working farms in 2009 with a simple idea: bring live country music to the communities that help feed the country.
articles.body: Luke Bryan began taking his concerts to working farms in 2009 with a simple idea: bring live country music to the communities that help feed the country. By the close of his 17th Farm Tour in September 2026, the project had awarded 97 college scholarships and helped provide more than 11 million meals, according to Luke Bryan’s official website and a report by AG Daily on Yahoo Entertainment.The 2026 edition continued the tour’s long-running partnership with Bayer through the #HerestotheFarmer campaign. It combined concerts in rural settings with practical support for farming families, local food banks and students pursuing higher education near the tour stops. Read more about it here:A tour built around farmsThe Farm Tour was created to put Bryan’s shows directly into agricultural communities rather than limiting them to arenas and amphitheatres. Since its launch in 2009, the tour has visited working farms across the United States, turning fields and farm properties into temporary concert venues. That setting matters because it keeps the music connected to the people and places it celebrates. Bryan’s audience is often made up of rural residents, agricultural workers and families whose livelihoods depend on farming, making the tour feel less like a travelling spectacle and more like a local gathering.The 2026 run marked the 17th Farm Tour and concluded in September. By that point, the initiative had grown from a novel concert format into a sustained programme with measurable benefits for students, food-insecure households and rural communities.Scholarships for farming familiesOne of the tour’s most lasting contributions has been its scholarship programme. Since 2009, Bryan has awarded 97 college scholarships to students from farming families who are attending local colleges or universities near Farm Tour stops. The scholarships are designed to support young people with direct ties to agriculture, helping ease the financial pressure that can come with pursuing education while remaining connected to family farms. Rather than offering one-off publicity moments, the programme has built a long record of investment in rural students. For many recipients, the support may make the difference between attending college and putting those plans aside. The scale of the programme, with nearly 100 scholarships awarded across 17 years, shows how a touring artist can turn a concert series into an ongoing educational resource.More than 11 million mealsThe tour’s food-security work has been equally significant. Through Bayer’s #HerestotheFarmer campaign, Bryan’s Farm Tour has helped provide more than 11 million meals, according to the artist’s official announcement.The campaign focuses on raising awareness, educating communities and expanding access to nutritious food, vitamins and minerals. It also mobilises concertgoers to support local food banks, connecting fans directly with hunger-relief organisations in the areas where the shows take place.During Farm Tour events, Bryan and Bayer have encouraged thousands of attendees to donate to local food banks. The approach turns each concert into an opportunity for collective action, with fans contributing to families facing food insecurity in their own communities.Fans contributed food tooThe 2026 tour also included on-site food collections, with fans donating nearly 20,000 pounds of nonperishable food so far. Those contributions are intended to provide meals through regional hunger-relief organisations.FFA chapters partnered with Bayer on the “Spirit of 1776” CAN DO Challenge, which generated donations of more than 10,000 cans for local food banks. The initiative brought student agricultural organisations into the effort, extending its reach beyond the concert crowds.Together, the food drives and corporate campaign illustrate how the Farm Tour operates on several levels at once. It entertains audiences, supports farmers, funds education and channels practical resources toward people who need them most.A broader commitment to communityBryan’s Farm Tour has become one of the more distinctive examples of a major artist using a tour for community impact. Instead of treating charitable work as an add-on, the project has made rural support a central part of its identity since its first edition in 2009.The scholarship programme and meal campaign also reflect a broader understanding of what rural communities need. Access to education, reliable food supplies and local support networks all affect the long-term health of farming families and the towns around them.By working with Bayer, FFA chapters and local food banks, Bryan has created a model that involves artists, fans, businesses and community organisations. The result is a programme whose impact extends well beyond the nights when the stage lights come on.The 2026 tour in contextThe Farm Tour concluded in September, while Bryan’s wider 2026 “Word On The Street Tour” wrapped in October after playing more than 35 cities. Produced by Live Nation, the broader tour included a sold-out Nashville show at Bridgestone Arena, Bryan’s seventh consecutive sold-out performance at that venue.The Farm Tour remains distinct from that arena-focused run because of its rural setting and community-first mission. It has allowed Bryan to reach audiences in places that larger tours may overlook, while also directing resources toward the people who live and work there.As the Farm Tour enters its next chapter, its legacy is already substantial. Ninety-seven scholarships, more than 11 million meals and nearly 20,000 pounds of donated food represent more than impressive totals; they show how a long-running concert project can become part of the social fabric of rural America.You use AI every day.
